hardware: 8-core Intel Core Ultra 5 236V dev container, Debian Trixie
name: v8malloc
workload: MB-01 single-thread alloc/write/free loop by size (8 B to 2 MiB) and MB-02 multi-thread 64 B ops/sec sweep, 1-8 threads.
claimed_speedup: 8 threads at 64 B: 296.4 M ops/s vs tcmalloc 290.8 M, glibc 295.2 M, jemalloc 271.3 M, mimalloc 217.5 M (mimalloc +36%); 4 threads 150.5 M vs glibc 134.9 M; single-thread 8 B 22 ns/op vs jemalloc 26, mimalloc 32. Trails tcmalloc at 16-256 KiB (about 60 vs 24 ns/op) and mimalloc on cross-thread free.
tradeoffs: Linux-only; NUMA-aware; mmap-heavy recycle cache for large blocks; project says in active development.
caveats: Single run per cell, README itself says single-digit-percent gaps are noise; most wins over glibc and tcmalloc are within 2%; clearly slower in the medium 16-256 KiB band and in producer/consumer; one-star project, benchmarks authored by the project; a concurrency bug in the core cache was fixed during the run.
found_via: WebSearch: new memory allocator research prototype source code outperforms mimalloc snmalloc 2025 OR 2024 paper github

name: Ralloc
workload: Threadtest, Shbench, Larson and other allocator microbenchmarks on persistent memory, recoverable lock-free allocator built on LRMalloc.
claimed_speedup: Per ISMM 2020 paper (seen via search snippet only): about 10x faster than Makalu and PMDK on Threadtest and Shbench, up to 37x faster than Makalu on Larson.
tradeoffs: Requires persistent memory or DRAM simulation via /dev/shm; C++11; needs filter functions for recovery, not supported in pure C; LRMalloc counter may overflow above 72 threads.
caveats: Paper PDF blocked here, numbers come from search snippets and could not be checked; baselines are persistent-memory allocators, not malloc/jemalloc (repo test harness can also compare jemalloc); last commit 2020.
found_via: WebSearch: persistent memory allocator github faster than PMDK libpmemobj OR Makalu OR Ralloc paper source

name: Mesh
workload: Firefox Speedometer, Redis fragmentation workload and SPEC CPU2006: peak RSS and runtime with Mesh's compacting (meshing) malloc replacement.
claimed_speedup: Reduces memory of Firefox by 16% and Redis by 39%; SPEC CPU2006 peak RSS 15% lower with 3.9% runtime overhead; runtime roughly equal to jemalloc (Redis insert 1.76 s vs 1.72 s). Not a speed win.
tradeoffs: Linux and macOS; relies on virtual-memory remapping; small runtime overhead; randomized allocation.
caveats: Win is memory footprint, not speed; PLDI 2019 paper (peer reviewed) not openable here, figures taken from search snippets; repo README has no benchmark numbers.
found_via: WebSearch: Mesh PLDI 2019 performance results Firefox Redis memory reduction runtime overhead versus jemalloc SPEC

name: NUMAlloc
baseline: mimalloc, glibc malloc, TcMalloc, Intel TBB
workload: Application benchmark suite on NUMA machines (ISMM 2023 paper).
claimed_speedup: 15.7% faster than the second-best allocator (mimalloc) and 20.9% faster than the default Linux allocator (a patent summary snippet gives 15.2% and 17.1%).
tradeoffs: NUMA-aware; reasonable memory overhead per paper; README lists planned work such as removing callsite info collection.
caveats: Peer-reviewed ISMM 2023 paper, ACM page blocked so numbers are from search snippets and differ between sources; license not confirmed on repo page I read.

name: Exgen-Malloc
workload: Single-threaded allocator tested on mimalloc-bench, SPEC CPU2017 and redis-benchmark.
claimed_speedup: 1.05x geometric mean over mimalloc on SPEC CPU2017 (another snippet says 1.03x), 1.17x over dlmalloc; 1.93x over dlmalloc on mimalloc-bench; 25.2% memory saving vs mimalloc on mimalloc-bench.
tradeoffs: Single-thread only, about 2000 lines, built by trimming mimalloc.
caveats: IEEE Computer Architecture Letters 2025 paper; arXiv and the PDF host were blocked, numbers from search snippets only; no repository link found.

name: LLFree
workload: Concurrent 4 KiB and 2 MiB page-frame allocation in a lock- and log-free allocator, plus compaction page movements.
claimed_speedup: Reduces allocation time for concurrent 4 KiB allocations by up to 88% and 2 MiB allocations by up to 98%; 64% fewer page movements in compaction (USENIX ATC 2023, per search snippet).
tradeoffs: Kernel page-frame allocator, not a userspace malloc; also available as Rust (llfree-rs) and a Linux tree.
caveats: Different baseline class from malloc; paper PDF blocked, numbers from snippet; repo page has no benchmark numbers.
found_via: WebSearch: LLFree allocator github luxitor llfree-rs OR llfree-c paper ATC 2023

name: LWMalloc
workload: Real applications on Raspberry Pi Zero W, Raspberry Pi 4 and Jetson Orin Nano (IEEE Internet of Things Journal 2025).
claimed_speedup: Up to 53% faster execution time and 23% lower memory than ptmalloc (search snippet and press release).
tradeoffs: About 530 lines, about 20 KB footprint; LD_PRELOAD injection; for resource-constrained devices.
caveats: Numbers only from search snippets; repo README has no numbers; license not seen on the page I read; compares to ptmalloc, not jemalloc or mimalloc.

name: elfmalloc
workload: Threadtest, Shbench and producer-consumer, 1 to 32 threads.
claimed_speedup: Highest throughput in most configurations, especially Shbench at high core counts; lags jemalloc at 32 threads on small objects; sometimes uses more memory (no single ratio given).
caveats: Author calls the evaluation preliminary; compiler flags not stated; no numbers extracted from charts; last commit date not confirmed.
